population.definition: Population of the City of Malabo enumerated in the 4th General Population and Housing Census (IV Censo de Población y Vivienda 2015) conducted by the Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Guinea Ecuatorial (INEGE), tabulated via CityPopulation. Bioko Norte Province as a whole recorded 300,374 residents.

facts.claim: Malabo was founded in 1827 as Port Clarence by British naval captain William Fitzwilliam Owen as a naval base to suppress the Atlantic slave trade and resettle liberated captives.

source.title: Equatorial Guinea: Provinces & Major Cities (Census 2015)
source.quote: Founded in 1827 as Port Clarence before becoming Santa Isabel and later Malabo

facts.claim: The Catedral de Santa Isabel de Malabo, designed by architect Luis Segarra Llairadó and consecrated in 1916, is a prominent Spanish colonial Neo-Gothic cathedral featuring twin 40-metre spires.

source.title: Catedral de Santa Isabel de Malabo: Arquitectura neogótica colonial
source.quote: Catedral neogótica consagrada en 1916 con torres de 40 metros

facts.claim: In 1973, the city of Santa Isabel was officially rechristened Malabo in honour of King Malabo Löpèlo Mëlaka, the last traditional Bubi monarch of Bioko Island.

source.title: Equatorial Guinea: Provinces & Major Cities (Census 2015)
source.quote: Renamed Malabo in 1973 after the Bubi king Malabo
